s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling of the manubrium with a history of previous thyroid surgery
salient_findings: Lytic lesion replacing the manubrium on CT imaging
Follicular thyroid cells on fine-needle aspiration
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
Previous resection of a large left substernal thyroid lobe 12 years ago
Swelling of the manubrium is slightly tender
Swelling increased in size over the month prior to presentation
CT imaging shows a lytic lesion replacing the manubrium
Residual right goiter is present
Lytic lesion is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein
Fine-needle aspiration revealed follicular thyroid cells
Pathological examination shows thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae

shortlist.label: follicular thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: history of previous thyroid surgery and presence of follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion

shortlist.label: nodular goiter
shortlist.why_kept: residual right goiter is present and patient has a history of previous thyroid surgery

shortlist.label: metastases
shortlist.why_kept: lytic lesion replacing the manubrium and presence of follicular thyroid cells

shortlist.label: adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: lytic lesion and history of previous thyroid surgery

shortlist.label: high flow arteriovenous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: lytic lesion in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein

raw.rationale: The presence of a lytic lesion in the manubrium with follicular thyroid cells on fine-needle aspiration and pathological examination showing thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae, along with a history of previous substernal thyroid lobe resection, supports the diagnosis of follicular thyroid carcinoma, which is known for its potential to metastasize to bone and present with lytic lesions.

rejected.label: nodular goiter
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of goiter, the presence of a lytic lesion and follicular thyroid cells infiltrating bone trabeculae suggests a more aggressive process than a simple goiter.

rejected.label: metastases
rejected.why: Metastases are a consideration, but the specific finding of follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion points more directly to a primary thyroid malignancy rather than metastasis from another source.

rejected.label: adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: Adenocarcinoma is a broad category of cancers, and while follicular thyroid carcinoma is a type of adenocarcinoma, the specific diagnosis of follicular thyroid carcinoma is more precise and directly supported by the evidence.

rejected.label: high flow arteriovenous malformation
rejected.why: The clinical and imaging findings do not support a vascular malformation; instead, they point towards a neoplastic process involving thyroid tissue.
